scene: 8 — Ada reallocates, and the numbers move
detail: The reallocation's outcome has no renderer. services/exceptions.py:185-243 already implements the right idea — an exception whose node has an undelivered inbound reallocation is ANSWERED (not resolved), carries {action_id, effect, actor, rationale}, and sorts to the bottom of the queue — and bootstrap.py:254 ships it to the client in world['exceptions']. But grep for `answered_by` across the whole repo returns only the two lines in exceptions.py that create and sort on it: no template, no JSX, no test reads it. On camera the consequence is that after Ada submits, the El Fasher exception is still rank 1, byte-identical, with its 'Reallocate to El Fasher Distribution Hub' button still live — inviting a second click on a problem already acted on. The row also failed to re-sort even though the map's consignment count refreshed 16→17, which points at a partial refetch of the world payload.
fix_recommendation: Render answered_by on the exception card: an 'Answered by <actor> — <effect>' block quoting the recorded rationale and action id, plus a visible demoted/answered treatment on the row. Then confirm the action's success handler refetches world['exceptions'] so the server-side demotion actually reaches the screen.

scene: 8 — Ada reallocates, and the numbers move
detail: The narration promises four outcomes and the product deliberately refuses three of them. 'El Fasher's weeks of cover moves out of the red' and 'the pipeline gap for that corridor closes' cannot happen, and should not: the new consignment is created with status PLANNED and the cartons have not arrived, so cover and the delivered-gap correctly stay put. That restraint is the app's own load-bearing invariant and is a stronger claim than the one being made. The narration is wrong here, not the model. Spine item S5 is status GAP and the walkthrough is narrating past it.
fix_recommendation: Either (a) re-narrate scene 8 to what actually happens — a real consignment against a named contract, the exception marked answered by the action that answers it and demoted below the ones nobody has touched, and the children still at risk until the truck lands; or (b) change the target: reallocate against the Komadugu partner shortfall instead. That row IS a ShortfallSignal, so actions.reallocate's `signal` branch fires, resolved_by_action is set, the exception genuinely resolves, and scenes 7 and 8 close the partner loop that why_brief S6 exists to make.

scene: 6 — Twelve thousand children, by the ninth of September
detail: The queue's stated premise is that every row is ranked in one unit — children who miss a full course. Two of the seven rows (SHP-2026-0302, 2 days behind into Maiduguri; SHP-2026-0402, 6 days behind into Djibo) print only a days-behind headline and carry no children figure at all, reverting to exactly the status-board framing the narrative rejects. Independent arithmetic confirms these rows are genuinely 0: the five stated figures sum to 1,087+240+87+60+47 = 1,521, exactly the 'Children at risk' KPI. cover.children_at_risk returns 0 when the delay is absorbed by stock on hand. So the ranking is correct and defensible — a 6-day delay ranked below a 1-day delay because the receiving node has cover — and the product hides its single most persuasive argument by printing nothing.
fix_recommendation: Render the zero explicitly on rows whose consequence is nil: '0 children lose a full course — the delay is absorbed by N weeks of cover on hand at <node>'. Keep the unit on every row so the ordering is self-evidently one ordering.

scene: 6 — Twelve thousand children, by the ninth of September
detail: The concept_claim says all FOUR exception kinds are ranked in one unit and the narration explicitly describes an expiry-risk row 'below the late consignments — cartons sitting where the caseload is too small to work through them before they expire'. No such row exists: the queue holds Late (x4), Short receipt (x2) and Partner shortfall (x1). The capability is real — cover.expiry_risk and exceptions.expiry_exceptions are implemented and unit-tested in test_cover.py — but the demo's only visible lot expires Jan 19 2028, far outside the 180-day horizon, so the exception can never fire. This is a seed-data gap, not a capability gap.
fix_recommendation: Seed a short-dated lot at an over-supplied node so expiry_exceptions fires — Soum's nodes are the natural home, since the coverage table already shows Soum at 145.8% of need, which is precisely the 'stock where the caseload is too small to consume it' case the narration describes.

scene: 6 — Twelve thousand children, by the ninth of September

fix_recommendation: Set the derivation as a readable sentence at body weight rather than small italic, use a proper multiplication sign, and render '0 weeks of cover' rather than '0.0'.

scene: 3 — Late is a measurement, not an argument
detail: The scene's entire concept_claim is that planned, estimated and actual are kept as three separate timestamps per milestone. The card's own subtitle reads 'Planned, estimated and actual — the three are never collapsed.' Every row shows exactly ONE date. Verified in source: shipment_detail.jsx:100-102 renders a ternary — `m.actual_at ? 'Actual X' : 'Planned X'` — and `estimated_at` is never rendered anywhere in the file. The final leg reads 'Arrive · El Fasher Distribution Hub / Planned Jul 28, 2026 · +9d vs plan', which is self-contradictory on its face: a date labelled Planned cannot be +9d against plan, and the estimated date (~6 Aug) that would make the delta subtractable is not on screen. The model keeps three; the UI shows one.
fix_recommendation: Render all three values in the rail row — Planned <date> · Estimated <date> · Actual <date or em-dash> — so the +9d delta can be verified by subtracting two dates the viewer can see. This is the whole point of the scene and the data is already on the model.

scene: 3 — Late is a measurement, not an argument

scene: 4 — Nobody can clear a red row by editing a field
detail: Scored once for the whole walkthrough and attached to its most emblematic scene. The use case is genuinely substantive — a multi-country famine response, real caseload denominators, exceptions ranked in children rather than tonnage, a reallocation requiring a recorded reason. It is held to 3 by the rubric's rule that the feature is never shown at the scale where its value would be felt, and scene 4 is the clearest instance: the append-only event log, which the why_brief calls 'the load-bearing invariant of this app', is demonstrated on a table containing exactly ONE row, from exactly one source tier ('Phone check-in'), with an em-dash for its quantity. A single entry cannot show accumulation, cannot show that nothing was edited, and cannot show the provenance variety that scene 2 spent its whole narration on. The payoff scene compounds it by exercising the reallocation on the one exception kind whose resolution the model cannot express.
fix_recommendation: Redraft what the walkthrough demonstrates: pick a consignment further along its route whose event log carries several actual events across at least two source tiers, so append-only accumulation and mixed provenance are both visible in one frame — and let the log visibly be where scene 2's three tiers pay off, rather than a card that mentions one.

scene: 1 — Which children are about to go without
detail: Judge-of-record finding; the per-scene judge did not run the cross-card arithmetic. The KPI row reads '115,170 Delivered to date / 1589 MT · 115,170 children treated'. That figure is the sum of the corridor DELIVERED column (43,782 + 15,000 + 36,000 + 20,388), i.e. cartons arrived at contract destinations — one of which is Port Sudan, a port, not a district. The Requirement-from-caseload card on the same page totals 48,787 courses delivered into districts against a requirement of 129,760, leaving 82,857 children with no carton assigned. So the same screen simultaneously claims 115,170 children treated and 82,857 children uncovered out of 129,760 needed. Glossing an arrivals figure as 'children treated' is also an outcome claim the delivery data cannot support, and it undercuts the exact argument scene 5 exists to make.
fix_recommendation: Drop the '· 115,170 children treated' gloss from the KPI and label it as cartons delivered against contract, or re-point it at the coverage card's courses-delivered-into-districts figure so the two cards reconcile.

scene: 1 — Which children are about to go without

fix_recommendation: Standardise button semantics — solid for the single recommended action, outline for secondary — across all exception kinds, and drop the duplicated stat line so more of the ranked queue fits in one viewport.
